title: Agentic Close After Ramp Spend | Flow ERP
summary: Flow ERP takes the next step after Ramp: entity-mapped books plus agents that help reconcile, review, explain, and close.
body_markdown:
After Ramp controls spend, agents help you close: that is the spend-to-truth story. Ramp stops bad outflow. Flow Agentic Accounting Platform takes the next step with entity-mapped books plus agents that help reconcile, review, explain, and close so controllers are not rebuilding CSVs every month-end.


## Key takeaways


-


**Spend control is not close complete.** Cards and bills still need to land in the right entity books with a reviewable trail.


-


**Native Ramp sync feeds the ledger.** Receipts, memos, and lifecycle updates (including refunds and voids) should travel with the transaction.


-


**Agent jobs matter post-sync.** Reconcile exceptions, review queues, explanations for operators, and close support.


-


**Multi-entity review queues scale better than inbox archaeology.** Mis-maps and missing docs should surface by entity, not in a single dump.


-


**Search name:** Flow ERP. **On-page:** Flow Agentic Accounting Platform.


## Spend control is not the same as close complete


Ramp is excellent at controlling who can spend and capturing documentation at the point of purchase. That is necessary and still incomplete for accounting. Close needs postings in the correct entity, intercompany clarity when one entity pays for another, and reporting leadership can trust without a spreadsheet rebuild.


Teams that stop at “we have Ramp” usually feel the gap in the last week of the month: exports, manual entity tags, and a reconciliation queue that grows with every new subsidiary. Partnership framing:[The Agentic Accounting Platform for Ramp Customers](https://www.liveflow.com/partners/ramp) .


## What flows in from Ramp


With Flow’s native Ramp connection, the practical ingest path is:


1.


Connect and authorize Ramp from Integrations in Flow.


2.


Configure entity mapping so each card or bill has a home.


3.


Sync in real time, including receipts and memos.


4.


Let refunds, cancellations, and voids follow the Ramp lifecycle into the books.


Full how-to and FAQ:[/integrations/ramp](https://www.liveflow.com/integrations/ramp) . Step-level mapping narrative:[Ramp multi-entity spend in Flow](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/ramp-multi-entity-spend-in-flow) .


## Which agent jobs matter after sync


Agentic accounting here is not a chatbot on a CSV. In Flow Agentic Accounting Platform, agents help with post-transaction work on top of synced Ramp data:


-


**Reconcile:** Match expected spend to postings and flag breaks early.


-


**Review:** Queue unusual vendors, missing receipts, or coding that needs a human.


-


**Explain:** Turn activity into answers controllers can share with operators.


-


**Close:** Reduce manual glue so month-end is review-heavy, not copy-paste-heavy.


Humans remain accountable for sign-off. Agents shrink the busywork between “Ramp recorded it” and “books are reportable.” Pillar context:[best agentic multi-entity accounting for Ramp](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/best-agentic-multi-entity-accounting-for-ramp) .


## Multi-entity review queues


When several legal entities share a Ramp program, exceptions should not land in one undifferentiated inbox. Controllers need to see mis-maps, missing docs, and odd merchants in the entity where the spend belongs. That is why entity mapping at setup is the make-or-break step, and why agent review queues sit on entity-mapped books rather than a catch-all company file.


If you are comparing a heavy ERP stack to Flow for this wedge, read[Ramp + Flow vs NetSuite for multi-entity teams](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/ramp-flow-vs-netsuite-multi-entity) . Construction-heavy groups can also use[construction spend on Ramp, books on Flow](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/construction-ramp-flow-multi-entity) .


## How to put spend-to-truth into practice


1.


Confirm Ramp is connected and entity mapping is explicit for every active spender.


2.


Run a daily light review of new exceptions (missing receipt, odd merchant, unmapped coding).


3.


Clear refunds and voids the same day they appear so jobs and entities stay honest.


4.


Use agent queues to prioritize human review before close starts, not after.


5.


Report from entity and consolidated views without waiting on a Ramp CSV.


Product home:[/flow](https://www.liveflow.com/flow) . Multi-entity hub:[multi-entity accounting and consolidation](https://www.liveflow.com/multi-entity-accounting-consolidation) .


## Frequently asked questions


Short answers for teams that already run Ramp and want a cleaner close.


## Does Ramp alone close the books?


No. Ramp controls spend and captures documentation. Closing still requires entity-correct postings, review, and reporting in an accounting system. Flow Agentic Accounting Platform is built for that next step with native Ramp sync.


## What do agents actually do after Ramp sync?


They help reconcile, review exceptions, explain activity, and support close on top of entity-mapped books. Controllers stay responsible for judgment and sign-off.


## Do receipts and voids come through with the spend?


Yes on the native path: receipts and memos sync with transactions, and refunds or voids in Ramp are reflected so books do not keep spend that no longer exists. Details:[Ramp integration](https://www.liveflow.com/integrations/ramp) .


## Is this only for multi-entity teams?


Single-entity teams can still benefit from native sync. Multi-entity groups feel the pain first when exports and separate company files break at close. Flow is designed with multi-entity as a first-class model.


## What is Flow ERP vs Agentic Accounting Platform?


Same product. Flow ERP appears in search titles, meta, and schema. On-page marketing uses Agentic Accounting Platform / Flow Agentic Accounting Platform.
